newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea crudes slump under pressure, outright soft.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea crudes slump under pressure, outright soft.

text.p: North Sea crudes were under severe pressure on Tuesday as Brent looked set to trade at ever falling levels and, with some other grades under prompt pressure, even sellers could not defend an imminent fall in premiums.
December Brent on the IPE traded at 1629 GMT down 43 cents at $23.75 a barrel.
There were three Brent cargoes in the paper chains (including one deferred from Monday following a five o'clocking) and traders expected more five o'clockings today.
Two November loading Brent cargoes were offered at December -10 cents, with sellers seeing little interest and traders expecting the next deal to be around December -20 cents.
Other grades under pressure included Statfjord with one offered around November 8 and another two days later. Many expected the former to trade as low as or even below Dated Brent +10 cents.
"This market is going south. There is nothing but black clouds around," one equity holder said.
"No one is offering a number -- everyone is asking for bids," a seller said.
Brent Nov/Dec talked around +22/25 cents, while Dec/Jan moved at +45 cents.
Intermonth spreads lost ground with next week moving at December -12 cents and offered again at that level.
